title: spiral-rollout-regional-decoupling-controller
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Existing region-by-region rollouts and blue/green flows are brittle when traffic spikes or when capacity mismatches occur. We need an automated controller and upgrade tooling that executes a deterministic spiral-style rollout: progressive, overlapping regional decoupling that moves a small, time-bounded weight slice through regions in a repeatable pattern. The spiral approach reduces large simultaneous shifts and minimizes global tail risk while enabling faster per-region completion than purely sequential canaries.

Proposal: Implement a Spiral Rollout Controller (SRC) integrated with the Host API gateway and the release orchestrator. The controller will: 1) accept a release bundle (model version, runtime tag, LTS channel target) and a spiral plan (region ordering, base step weight, step duration, overlap window); 2) translate the plan into per-region traffic deltas and orchestrate weighted shifts via the routing API; 3) attach SLO gates and observability checks to each step (latency percentiles, error rate, token cost delta, tail p99p999); 4) support automatic backoff and partial rollback heuristics plus a manual operator override path; 5) ensure LTS channel constraints (only move tenants pinned to the target LTS or in opt-in bucket) and surface a preflight validation report to the console.

Key design points: 
- Weight decay semantics: each step moves an absolute weight (e.g., 2%) plus a decay value to remove old version traffic in preceding regions. Overlaps between adjacent regions are configurable to allow warm KV caches.
- Safety gates: multi-metric SLO evaluation window (30s, 5m, 15m) with configurable thresholds; a single breached gate pauses and can auto-backoff to a safe weight.
- Rollout spirals are parameterizable: regional priority lists, step velocity, and maximum in-flight regions.
- Integration with existing features: ties into the existing rollout audit log, the Console rollout timeline, and the release tracker for LTS and pinning.
- Upgrade tooling: add a preflight job that runs canary traffic against a synthetic prompt-set (evangelized prompts), verifies tokenization/quantization compatibility, runs KV cache warmup probes, and publishes a human-readable checklist.

Trade-offs: Spiral reduces simultaneous risk at the cost of longer wall-clock completion for global rollout. More overlap increases cache warmness but raises transient dual-version resource utilization. We prioritize SLO safety and predictable operator control over raw speed for hosted customers.

Implementation plan: 
- Phase 1 (2 sprints): controller core, routing API extension for staged weight plans, small e2e test harness in staging.
- Phase 2 (2 sprints): SLO gate engine, console UX for spiral plan creation, preflight job.
- Phase 3 (1 sprint): production canary with low-risk LTS channel (opt-in customers), iterate on thresholds and rollback heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can consume a spiral plan and emit per-region weighted shift events to routing API
Controller honors LTS channel pinning and only targets eligible tenants/regions
SLO gate evaluates latency and error-rate metrics and pauses rollout on breach
Preflight synthetic check runs and emits a pass/fail checklist to the Console
Operator can perform immediate abort and selective rollback via the Console and CLI
End-to-end test demonstrates a safe spiral rollout in staging with no SLO regressions

notes: Operator story: named plan -> dry-run -> approve -> execute -> monitor -> finalize
Rollback heuristics: exponential backoff then shrink to last-known-good weight, then full rollback if persistent breach
We will reuse existing rollout audit schema but add spiral_plan_id and step_id fields (schema change documented in PR)
